newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump at close on profit-taking, Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump at close on profit-taking, Dow.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended their midday slide at the close on Friday as profit-taking continued after a late downward turn on Wall Street, traders and analysts said.

"Volatile Dow industrials and high U.S. GDP figures led to uncertainty in the run-up to the forthcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting. Investors were cautious and most decided to liquidate stocks," said Esteban Rojas, deputy director of equity analysis at the Arka brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended down 25.75 points, or 0.70 percent, at 3,647.17.
Analysts nonetheless stressed the bourse's underlying strength and said it was still in a short-term upward channel.

"The market is still validating a consolidation zone between 3,600 and 3,750 points. Although it was listless today, it did not break through floor level at 3,630 points," said Leonor Gonzalez, a technical analyst at the BBV-Probursa brokerage.
Volume was down from Thursday's levels to an unremarkable 90.97 million shares traded.
On the broad market, a total of 103 stocks changed hands, of which 54 were down while 38 were ahead.
Financial groups Serfin and Inverlat topped the gainers' list, up 20 and four centavos, respectively, to 3.20 pesos and 69 centavos.
"Serfin and Inverlat gained because the market had hit them hard after the first financial groups posted 1996 earnings, and they were well-priced for day-trippers," a floor trader said.
Traders added that the presence of illiquid stocks among percentage gainers was a sign the market was running out of steam.
The decliners' list was led by stocks that had lagged the market, traders added.
Mining and autoparts company San Luis headed the decliners, followed by bus and truck maker Dina, which fell 1.30 pesos and 0.24 centavos, respectively, to 16.50 and 5.76 pesos.
